blocker.summary: The safe base is the accepted M17 point and contains no integrated M18 browser API, so guest navigation, network, tabs, durable browser state, transfers, clipboard, and IME cannot be driven from this branch without importing other owners' unfinished production work. The first M18-C hosted run exposed and recorded a feature-graph parser bug; a correction has passed focused local tests and awaits hosted retry. The local M17 feature graph remains unavailable because third_party/cc-nagi was not fetched on this macOS host.
blocker.failure_log_summary: Hosted CI run 36409153587 at head 9cf9d40272fd29b4b8821620907b62f0fa2d3d35: `M18-C M17 feature-off acceptance and target report` failed with `M17 graph did not include expected nodes: nagi-init feature "m17-servo"`; the actual cargo tree command succeeded. The follow-up target report emitted FAIL and the upload-artifact step succeeded. Root cause: cargo tree does not print the requested root feature as a separate node; corrected by checking the selected nagi-init root package and nagi-albert presence while retaining the explicit --features m17-servo command argument. Local cargo tree still reports `failed to read third_party/cc-nagi/Cargo.toml: No such file or directory`; earlier pinned fetch attempts could not populate the dependency due host toolchain/Apple xcrun architecture errors. Guest product cases remain SKIP-BLOCKED with owners in cases.json. M18-A CI run 36386094625 failed at remote web acceptance; M18-B run 36375495228 passed its current chrome acceptance. The M18 main integration checkout is separate and dirty, so it was not used as a base.
attempted_fixes: Selected exact base 94e9a027618182b10c0ac2315e94673543f22423, the shared M18 starting point immediately after the accepted M17 run, to avoid importing separate/unfinished M18-A/B product changes.
Added deterministic local HTTP/HTTPS, redirect, timeout, error, transfer, and storage/recovery inputs; all 30 M18-C focused tests pass.
Changed malformed HTTP fixture to an invalid status line after the host HTTP client accepted the original malformed Content-Length case.
Fixed recovery-fixture tests after they exposed missing pathlib import and temporary-directory lifetime errors; the final focused rerun passed.
Attempted local pinned dependency fetch and target feature graph inspection; retained explicit BLOCKED evidence instead of treating the missing graph as a pass.

Recorded hosted run 36409153587's feature-gate failure; removed the invalid expectation that cargo tree list the root m17-servo feature as an independent node, and added regression coverage for its actual output shape plus explicit leak rejection.

Do not merge, rebase, or force-push this branch, and do not widen work into M19-PREP or 0.2.

acceptance_criteria: A deterministic local HTTP/HTTPS fixture server covers direct pages, redirects, redirect loops, status errors, connection refusal, timeout, malformed responses, TLS verification, download, and upload.

Deterministic state fixture inputs exist for missing, empty, clean multi-tab, truncated, malformed, incompatible-version, partial-record, interrupted-write, and repeated-restore scenarios without defining or implementing the production storage API.
The 34-case report validates evidence identifiers, statuses, proof, ownership, blocked reasons, and overall PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL rules.
CI produces host and target acceptance reports and uploads them even when the corresponding focused checks fail or omit evidence.
The M17 target feature graph must prove M18-only browser features are absent; the M18-on graph remains integration-owned until a shared M18 target entry point exists.
No M18-A, M18-B, M18 main, M19-PREP, or 0.2 product implementation is added by this workstream.
All required guest-facing acceptance cases must pass on the integrated M18 implementation before this state can become PASS.
